A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViGiL3D study. Their main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, pipeline validation, human grounding accuracy, and experiments evaluating seven grounding methods.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds fuller linguistic-property results and qualitative observations from VLM prompt-generation trials.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o/spaCy analysis pipeline, analysis prompts in Listings 1–3, and grounding implementations are unchanged. Expanded annotation explanations and the new architecture diagram do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Section 7 newly reports qualitative trials of VLMs generating grounding descriptions from images, captions, and scene graphs, adding an ancillary generation task. The 350-prompt ScanNet/ScanNet++ grounding benchmark and eight prior datasets analyzed remain unchanged.

E2.justification: OpenScene, LERF, ZSVG3D, LLM-Grounder, 3D-VisTA, 3D-GRAND, and PQ3D retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. Newly cited scene-graph methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the reported pipeline-validation scope from 24 to 28 binary metrics and describes 35 criteria overall. Appendix A.4 still says 24, leaving the actual validation scope unresolved. The retained grounding settings, sample counts, and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7 adds qualitative failure analysis from VLM prompt-generation trials, covering cross-view reasoning, insufficient diversity, and descriptions that fail to distinguish targets. The subgroup, GT-versus-Mask3D, ScanNet++, and reweighted analyses already appeared in v1.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 retains the same two-tailed two-proportion z-test and statistical-analysis discussion. No new confidence intervals, uncertainty estimates, seed information, or independent-run reporting are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 10–12 add previously unreported linguistic-property entries, including additional attribute, relationship, and reference categories. Section 7 adds qualitative VLM failure findings. Retained grounding scores, the 84% human accuracy, and the reported 0.18-to-0.19 reweighting result are unchanged.

T1.justification: The linguistic taxonomy and grounding metric definitions are retained. Table 1 reorganizes existing criteria; neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs that are added or revised in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract and central dataset/performance claims remain unchanged. The introduction adds an explicit novelty distinction: the analysis pipeline categorizes attributes and relationships and identifies higher-level linguistic patterns beyond those captured by existing scene-graph extraction methods.

C2.justification: The brief small-dataset limitation expands into a substantive account of obstacles to VLM-based scaling: weak cross-view and viewpoint reasoning, dependence on in-context examples, diversity–correctness tradeoffs, and inadequate target discrimination. v2 explicitly conditions future scaling on overcoming these limitations.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly explains how annotators constructed zero-target prompts by modifying descriptions of existing objects. Appendix B.2 clarifies that human evaluators received the same ground-truth object segmentations as the models. These are disclosures about retained work, without evidence of changed annotation or evaluation runs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sun et al., Qian et al., and Gu et al. to distinguish its linguistic analysis from scene-graph extraction, and Chang et al. to support discussion of VLM generation diversity. The main related-work survey otherwise remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction gains contribution bullets, dataset-rationale and limitations passages expand, and several explanations and cross-references are edited. The section hierarchy and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 1 and substantially expands the visual presentation with dataset and model radar charts, a model-family architecture diagram, and full linguistic-comparison Tables 10–12. Table 1 is reorganized and floats are relocated. The former qualitative Figures 4–5 remain as Figures 7–8.

improvement.justification: The fuller linguistic-property tables provide evidence omitted from v1, while annotation and human-evaluation clarifications improve transparency. The expanded positioning and scaling limitations also help readers assess the contribution. Gains are limited by unchanged core experiments, underspecified VLM trials, and the conflicting validation-metric counts in Section 3.1 and Appendix A.4.
